compiler.stdout:
on1xc - a small strict ML-family frontend targeting ISO C11
usage: on1xc [--check | --emit-c | --tokens | --types | --emit-ast] INPUT.on1x [-o OUTPUT]
       on1xc --check-interfaces INPUT.on1x --interface FILE.on1xi [--interface FILE.on1xi ...]
       [--ppx LABEL PROGRAM] [--ppx-schema LABEL FILE] [--allow-source-ppx]
       [--ppx-timeout-ms MILLISECONDS]
       [--enable NAME[,NAME]] [--disable NAME] (bundled native extensions only)
       on1xc --list-extensions | --explain-extension NAME
       on1xc --emit-category-plan INPUT [-o OUTPUT] (checked concrete evidence)
       on1xc --kernel-imports INPUT [-o OUTPUT] (source requests only; never executes PPX)
       on1xc --emit-c --kernel-c11 INPUT (unsafe KernelBind C generation; link with on1x-build.py)
       on1xc --emit-c --kernel-c11 --kernel-stage INPUT (unresolved kernel callers; NOT admission)
       [-I DIRECTORY | --module-path DIRECTORY] [--stdlib DIRECTORY]
       [--lib-path DIR:DIR] [--stdlib-path DIR:DIR]
       [--ppx-path DIR:DIR] [--stdppx-path DIR:DIR] [--use-ppx NAME]
       on1xc --print-stdlib (resolved first standard-library root)
       on1xc --stdlib-resource RELATIVE_PATH (find a standard-library resource)
       [--no-prelude] [--prelude FILE] [--stdppx PROCESSOR]
       on1xc --deps INPUT.on1x [-o OUTPUT] (dependency paths, no PPX execution)
       on1xc [--emit-ir | --emit-ir-c | --ir-cfg | --run-ir] INPUT [-o OUTPUT] [--ir-input]
       on1xc --sdk-analyze NAME|linked-v2:HOOK INPUT [--ir-input]
       on1xc --sdk-emit NAME INPUT [-o OUTPUT] [--ir-input]
       on1xc --sdk-emit mir-archon --sdk-target TRIPLE INPUT [-o ASSEMBLY] [--ir-input] [--optimize-ir]
         native options: --native-pic --native-no-entry
       [--plugin +NAME_OR_PATH] (repeatable in SDK hook modes)
       on1xc sdk COMMAND [ARGS ...] (bounded SDK data tool)
       on1xc [--emit-ir-facts | --analyze-ir] INPUT [-o OUTPUT] [--ir-input]
       [--analysis-work UNITS] (Novostone opt-in build; --analyze-ir only)
       [--optimize-ir] [--opt-work UNITS] [--opt-rewrites COUNT] (MIR modes only)
       on1xc --dump-passes INPUT [-o OUTPUT] [--ir-input]
       on1xc --check-memory INPUT [-o OUTPUT] (Chisel opt-in build)
       [--admitted-extern FILE] (reviewed scalar-only extern evidence; memory modes only)
       [--memory-check] (check resource usage before source compilation)
       on1xc --check-types INPUT [-o OUTPUT] (Nerotypical opt-in build)
       [--verify-types] (require independent structural HIR type verification)
       [--diagnostics text|json|sarif] [--color auto|always|never] (diagnostics use stderr)
       [--diagnostic-catalog FILE] [--scrutiny LEVEL] [--project-scrutiny LEVEL]
       [--scrutiny-work UNITS] [--no-analysis-repairs] (bounded Wetstone analysis)
       on1xc --repair INPUT.on1x -o NEW_FILE (Syren; reviewable proposal only)
       on1xc --help
       on1xc init (--bin | --proj | --lib) [DIRECTORY]
       on1xc exec COMMAND [ARGS ...] (explicit On1xfile command execution)
       on1xc fmt INPUT [--target plain|latex|troff] [--check | --inplace | -i | -o OUTPUT]
       on1xc (--format | --emit-latex | --emit-troff) INPUT [-o OUTPUT]
--emit-ast expands macros and exports pre-PPX AST; it never executes programs.
MIR modes support i64/bool/void, direct On1x calls, control flow and scalar print/assert.
--run-ir is a bounded reference evaluator, not a native or VM backend.
--ir-input reads verified serialized MIR instead of On1x source (MIR modes only).
Output defaults to stdout. Use tools/on1x-build.py to link a native executable.
